scope: Remediation of the same-day full-codebase review. Working tree on main at e0a4464f.
status: Nine of fifteen tasks closed with local evidence. Four remain open as multi-week work, and two need an action only the repository owner can take.

findings.title: The tree does not pass its own build
findings.action: ktlintFormat on kms:plugins:hashicorp cleared all 232 violations across 10 files. The module baseline is unchanged, so nothing was grandfathered.

findings.title: main carries an unversioned copy of the reviewed code
findings.action: The tree is committed on main. Merging the codex/* remediation branches and pushing is left to the owner: it rewrites shared history and publishes the work.
findings.remaining: Merge codex/joint-remediation-20260910, push, confirm the CI run.

findings.title: There is no publication path
findings.status: Closed in code; one external step remains
findings.action: Declared a Maven repository in the root build and in the BOM, added scm and issueManagement to every POM, corrected the dead documentation URL, added a reviewer-gated publish job on v* tags, and added scripts/check-publication.py to CI so none of it can regress.
findings.evidence: publishAllPublicationsToCentralRepository now exists; 103 generated POMs validate
findings.remaining: Sonatype namespace verification and the secrets/environment setup in docs/operations/publishing.md.

findings.title: Coverage is bimodal
findings.remaining: 57.30% line / 39.83% branch to roughly 75% / 60%, top-down from credential-api. Two to three weeks of test writing; not attempted here.

findings.title: 61 dependency coordinates escape the catalog
findings.action: All 61 literals moved into gradle/libs.versions.toml across 34 build files. Converged web3j 4.10.0 to 4.14.0, gson 2.10.1 to 2.14.0, slf4j 2.0.9 to 2.0.17 and kotlinx-coroutines-test 1.8.1 to 1.10.2. bitcoinj stays at 0.16.2 through a new bitcoinj-legacy alias because 0.17 is a breaking API change that needs its own migration; the drift is now recorded in the catalog instead of hidden in a module. scripts/check-dependency-catalog.py fails the build on a new literal.
findings.evidence: 109 build scripts checked, zero literal coordinates; affected modules compile on the converged versions

findings.title: Three shipped servers have no authentication primitive
findings.action: Added HostAuthentication to the observability module: constant-time bearer tokens, host-supplied authorizers, an explicit frontedByProxy declaration, and per-caller fixed-window rate limiting with bounded caller tracking. The DID registrar, VC API and status-list servers gained withAuthentication and refuse mutating requests with 503 until it is called. This is a breaking change and is recorded in the changelog.
findings.evidence: 13 new tests in HostAuthenticationTest; ABI dumps updated additively

findings.title: Instrumentation stops at the HTTP boundary
findings.remaining: An observability SPI through did-core, kms-core, wallet-core and credential-api. One week; not attempted here.

findings.title: Half the workflows are unpinned
findings.action: All 14 remaining action references pinned to commit SHAs with version comments. Added permissions blocks to the two workflows that had none. The nightly conformance job's issues:write moved to a separate job that runs no repository code, so a compromised build dependency cannot reach it. scripts/check-workflow-pinning.py enforces both properties in CI.
findings.evidence: 6 workflows checked; every action SHA-pinned and every job permission-scoped

findings.title: Nothing is declared production-supported
findings.action: Added a ratchet: every module must appear in the capability catalog or in config/capability-ratchet.json, and the unassessed count may only fall. A new module with no declared maturity now fails the build.
findings.remaining: Classifying the 102 recorded modules, and the custody and hardware qualification behind a supported rating. Both are owner decisions, not mechanical work.

findings.title: A presenter-reachable exception escapes the verification contract
findings.action: ChainVerifier translates ledger IllegalStateException and IllegalArgumentException into an invalid result with a stable message, alongside the SQLException path it already had.
findings.evidence: New regression in IssuanceRoundTripTest drives both exception types through a refusing data source

findings.title: Two documented cancellation gaps
findings.action: encodeBitSet and decodeBitSet are suspend and call ensureActive() every 8192 bits, as their TODOs prescribed. updateCredentialStatus became suspend with them; every caller was already suspend, so no public signature changed.
findings.evidence: Two new tests: a cancelled revocation issues fewer statements than a completed one, proving the decode loop aborted before its post-decode SQL; and a structural guard that both functions stay suspend

findings.title: The validation gates read the wrong directory on Windows
findings.action: Added scripts/build_root.py, which resolves the build root the way the Gradle build does, including the trustweave.windowsInRepoBuild opt-out, and refuses a root holding no JUnit results rather than reporting phantom gaps. Both gates now use it.
findings.evidence: Both gates exit 0 with no arguments after a build; 9 unit tests cover the resolution and the refusal

findings.title: Broad catch surface
findings.status: Partially closed; the original count was wrong
findings.correction: The review said 549 broad catches with 12 empty bodies. The 549 is right (550 on a precise count). The 12 is not: a balanced-brace scan finds zero genuinely empty catch bodies and 21 whose body is only a comment. That figure came from a line-counting grep, not a parse.
findings.action: Of those 21, four sat in suspend functions and swallowed CancellationException: TrustedDomainManager.emitSafely, InMemoryDomainTreasury.emitSafely and two testkit integration helpers. All four now rethrow it. The rest are best-effort close() and logging fallbacks in non-suspend code, each already carrying a comment explaining why.
findings.remaining: 187 broad catches in suspend functions that neither rethrow nor convert to a result. Most are legitimate conversions to a sealed failure; the audit is a week's work and is not attempted here.

findings.title: Deployment-scale ledger qualification
findings.remaining: Sustained load, replica promotion under write load, published RPO/RTO. Needs real infrastructure and soak time.

findings.title: Compile the documentation consumers copy
findings.remaining: 9 of 2,363 Kotlin blocks are source-backed. One week; not attempted here.

new_gates: scripts/check-workflow-pinning.py — every action SHA-pinned, every job permission-scoped
scripts/check-dependency-catalog.py — no dependency version outside the catalog
scripts/check-publication.py — publishing repository declared, POMs complete, documentation links live
scripts/check-capability-coverage.py — every module declares a maturity; the unassessed count may only fall
scripts/build_root.py — evidence gates read the directory Gradle actually wrote
